MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your role at SJG Healthcare At Home

We are seeking applications from Senior Occupational Therapists to join our OT Rehab at Home service, on a casual roster with potential permanent positions available in the next 3 to 6 months. As a Senior Occupational Therapist - Grade 2 or 3 depending on your experience, you'll join a collaborative multidisciplinary team, delivering high-quality, client-centred occupational therapy services that empower people to achieve their goals and maintain independence in the comfort of their own homes.

This senior role offers the opportunity to apply your specialist clinical expertise, work independently, and influence best practice across the service. You'll also play a key role in mentoring and developing junior clinicians, supervising students, and contributing to education, quality improvement, and research initiatives that shape the future of care.

At St John of God Healthcare at Home, we're transforming the way healthcare is delivered. Our home visiting service enables people to recover from surgery or manage ongoing health needs in the familiar surroundings of their own home. By partnering with clients and their families, we provide personalised, flexible care that helps people feel safe, confident, and in control throughout their healthcare journey. From hospital-in-the-home programs to ongoing community-based support, you'll have the opportunity to deliver care where it matters most, making a lasting difference in the lives of those you support.

We are the At-Home Team for each of the SJOG hospitals across WA and work out of the Osborn Park Office, SJG Murdoch and SJG Midland hospitals to accommodate most metro areas.

This position will be offered on a casual basis with an expectation of 1-2 shifts weekly depending on caseload with potential permanent positions available in the next 3 to 6 months. 

The Position:

Provide Occupational Therapy treatment at a senior level.

Complete of comprehensive patient assessment (e.g. assessment of personal care, domestic and community ADLs, assessment of the home environment, cognitive and functional physical assessment as required).

Provide comprehensive treatment intervention and appropriate progression treatment to match functional goals to manage complex patients.

In conjunction with the Supervisor-Manager and other Occupational Therapy caregivers, develop processes for the evaluation of both inpatient and outpatient Occupational Therapy programs.

Put patients-clients plans in place and monitor outcomes regularly through attendance at and participation in multi-disciplinary team meetings.

Strive for high satisfaction levels of patients, clients and external agencies.

Complete appropriate administrative duties. Liaise with the administration team, report statistical data and ensure completion of progress notes.

Demonstrates consolidated, current knowledge of research, evidence based practice in Occupational Therapy and related clinical areas.

Act as a clinical consultant for the discipline and within the specialty.

Exercise independent professional judgment on routine matters. Obtain direct professional supervision from more senior caregivers when performing novel, complex or critical tasks.

We are looking for those who enjoy working collaboratively, are committed to continuous improvement and keen to contribute to innovative clinical practice while supporting the development of others. Strong communication and interpersonal skills will be essential for building positive relationships and working effectively with clients from diverse cultural, linguistic, and social backgrounds. Occupational Therapists with Rehab in the Home (RITH), community care and-or home visiting experience are encouraged to apply. Hospital experience is not necessary.

To succeed in this role, you will hold a Tertiary qualification in Occupational Therapy and current registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA). You'll bring senior clinical experience, ideally within healthcare or disability services, along with a passion for delivering evidence-based, persocentred care. A current driver's licence and Working With Children Card is essential for this community-based role.

Above all, patient care will be at the core of everything you do committing to and supporting our Mission and Values.

We can offer you

Casual Rate: $82.55 to $88.02 per hour (inclusive of casual loading) plus 12% superannuation

Casual position offering 1-2 shifts per week depending on case load

As a casual employee, you can salary package a percentage of your earnings each pay period A healthy work-life balance through flexible work options, additional purchased leave & well-being programs

Options to work out of SJG Murdoch, SJG Midland or Osborne Park

Employee discount on St John of God Hospital & Medical Services and Private Health Insurance

Employee support through our dedicated free Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

All applicants are asked to submit a current CV and covering letter (of no more than two (2) pages) demonstrating how you meet the above position requirements.

For enquiries contact Magdeleen Van Der Linde, Coordinator Rehabilitation at Home on 0497891929.

Applications will be reviewed throughout the advertising period and interviews conducted regularly. If suitable applicants are identified advertisement may close prior to listed date. Apply today!

At St John of God Health Care, we celebrate diversity and warmly welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. 

Our commitment is to create a safe and nurturing environment for all children and vulnerable individuals in our care and proactively take steps to protect them from abuse, ensuring their safety and well-being. 

Our inclusive culture fosters an environment that is respectful and secure, welcoming and accessible, and unified through our diverse community.

All caregivers employed by St John of God Health Care are required to be vaccinated from Influenza in order to fulfil the requirements of the role.    Click here to Apply now →

Objective
To be a key member of the Mission to Seafarers South Australia team, providing welfare services to visiting seafarers while supporting the sustainable development and operation of Mission to Seafarers centres across South Australia.
Based in Port Pirie, the Port Welfare Officers will share responsibility for providing seafarer welfare services, supporting volunteers and committees, coordinating administration, and assisting with the development of services in all South Australian ports, including Port Adelaide,  Port Lincoln, Port Giles, Thevenard, Wallaroo and any future centres established within the state.
The role combines practical seafarer welfare, volunteer coordination, administration, stakeholder engagement and centre development.

Level of Responsibility
The Port Welfare Officers report directly to the Regional Director, Mission to Seafarers Australia.
They work closely with the South Australian Management Committee, local port committees, volunteers, port authorities, shipping agents, churches and other stakeholders to ensure effective delivery of welfare services throughout the state.

The role shares responsibility for:
Day-to-day operation of the Port Pirie Seafarers Centre.
Development and support of Mission to Seafarers activities throughout South Australia.
Volunteer recruitment, training and support.
Administrative and financial management of the South Australian operations.
Regular travel to South Australian ports to visit ships, support volunteers and strengthen relationships with industry partners.

Conditions
The successful applicant will be required to maintain:
Current Driver's Licence.
National Police Check.
Safe Church Communities accreditation (or equivalent).
Working With Children Check (or applicable state screening requirements).
Australian Border Force and Port Security access requirements as required.
Capacity to travel throughout South Australia, including overnight travel where necessary.

About the Role
This position would suit someone who is passionate about improving the welfare of seafarers, enjoys working with volunteers and industry, is highly organised, flexible and self-motivated, and is comfortable working across multiple locations.
The role requires initiative, strong communication skills and the ability to build relationships with maritime industry stakeholders while developing sustainable welfare services across regional ports.

Knowledge and Experience
The successful applicant will possess excellent interpersonal and communication skills together with confidence using technology.
A sound working knowledge of Microsoft Office, Xero or similar accounting software, databases, social media and web-based systems is desirable.

Essential Skills and Experience
Office administration experience.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organisational and time management skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a small team.
Proficient in Microsoft Office.
Experience using accounting software (preferably Xero).
Experience coordinating volunteers or community programs.
Current driver's licence and willingness to travel.
Desirable Skills and Experience
Experience preparing agendas, minutes and financial reports.
Website and social media management.
Marketing and communications experience.
Fundraising and grant administration.
Community development experience.
Understanding of the Mission to Seafarers and the maritime industry.
Experience working with committees or not-for-profit organisations.

Duties and Responsibilities
1. Seafarer Welfare
Visit ships and provide welfare support to visiting seafarers.
Coordinate transport, shopping, communications and welfare services.
Supply SIM cards, Wi-Fi access and welfare items.
Assist with emergency welfare situations when required.
Promote compliance with the Maritime Labour Convention welfare provisions.
2. Centre and Port Development
Support the ongoing development of Mission to Seafarers services throughout South Australia.
Assist with establishing and growing welfare activities in new and developing ports.
Identify opportunities to improve facilities and services.
Build relationships with port authorities, shipping agents, terminal operators and industry stakeholders.
Promote awareness of seafarer welfare across the maritime community.
3. Administration
Prepare agendas, reports and committee meeting minutes.
Complete and maintain Australian Border Force documentation.
Maintain registrations, licences and compliance records.
Monitor donations and acknowledge supporters.
Support committee office bearers with administration.
Manage SIM cards, vouchers and foreign currency.
Assist the Regional Director with reporting and projects.
4. Communications and Marketing
Monitor incoming enquiries.
Coordinate communications with volunteers, shipping agents and port stakeholders.
Maintain websites and social media platforms.
Produce promotional material highlighting Mission activities.
Represent Mission to Seafarers at community and industry events.
5. Volunteer Management
Recruit new volunteers across South Australia.
Coordinate induction, training and mentoring.
Maintain volunteer records and compliance.
Coordinate Working With Children Checks, port inductions, First Aid and other required training.
Develop volunteer rosters where applicable.
6. Financial Administration
Assist with day-to-day financial administration.
Process invoices and expenses.
Support budgeting and financial reporting.
Maintain accurate records using Xero or equivalent systems.
7. Stakeholder Engagement
Develop productive relationships with:
Flinders Ports
Shipping agents
Maritime unions
AMSA
Australian Border Force
Port Welfare Committees
Local churches
Community organisations
Government agencies
Represent Mission to Seafarers at meetings and forums as required.
8. Attendance
Attend:
South Australian committee meetings.
National Mission to Seafarers conferences.
Volunteer training events.
Industry meetings and conferences.
Ship visits across South Australian ports.
Other duties as directed by the Regional Director.

Employment Conditions
The position is offered as a job-share arrangement, with two Port Welfare Officers working collaboratively to provide consistent coverage across South Australia.
The combined role is funded at 5Days per week, with flexibility to increase hours through project funding or centre development initiatives.
Regular travel throughout South Australia is an essential component of the role, with a Mission vehicle available where appropriate.
Comprehensive on-the-job training will be provided.
The role would suit someone with several years of workplace experience who enjoys working with people, is comfortable travelling, and wants to make a meaningful contribution to the wellbeing of international seafarers visiting South Australian ports.

Working out of our very cool Melbourne office, you will build your own accounts and networks. We will help you to develop your business and ensure your success as a best in class recruitment and technology professional.

You are able to work on both contract and permanent roles and you can build up significant revenue streams whilst placing permanent candidates. 

We have multiple positions available, such as:

- Candidate Manager 
- Associate Consultatant
- Recruitment Consultant
- Senior Consultant
- Managing Consultant
- Principal Consultant
- Client Services Manager 

Consultants within PRA are responsible to develop long term relationships with clients and to offer a professional and effective service to clients and candidates.  Delivery and the style of the delivery are paramount to maintain and develop the image of PRA as a leading supplier of recruitment solutions.
What will you do?
- Selling and promoting PRA’s services to existing and new customers
- Expanding PRA’s reach within each customer through business development activities
- Managing and maintaining client accounts for PRA’s services through consistent communication and client visits
- Assessing clients’ needs and providing services and solutions that satisfy client requirements
- Co-ordinating with PRA’s internal resources to ensure customers receive best in class service
- Providing timely and regular reporting to both internal and external stakeholders
- Utilising market knowledge to pitch new clients and win new business
- Dealing with clients & candidates, developing long term effective relationships
- Negotiating rates with clients, both contract and permanent
- Giving presentations to clients
- Handling clients and applicants through recruitment process to successful conclusion
- Writing advertisement copy
- Selection of applicants for vacancies
- Interviewing applicants
- Arranging interviews with clients and candidates
- Ensuring contact is made on a regular basis with contractors once placed out on the client’s site
- Maintaining awareness of trends within area of technical specialisation
- Ensuring that contact is made with clients on a regular basis and updating the database

What kind of person thrives in the PRA environment?   

Communication and people management are the defining elements of this role.  To perform it successfully, a candidate will need to be confident, and possess the ability to inform and persuade others and effectively present both themselves and the organisation they represent.  Friendliness and charisma are important factors in performing such a job effectively, together with the ability to put others at their ease.

Attention to detail, responsiveness and adaptability are also key elements in this job.  You will have energy and enthusiasm, and the ability to deal confidently with changes in work environments and situations.  The job often calls for work to meet deadlines or be completed within short timescales, and the ideal candidates will be prepared to commit themselves if they are to succeed.

Recruitment is challenging and fast-moving, and there are times you will practice patience to see through a difficult time or a minor repetitive task.  Having said this, you will see that these periods as necessary to your personal advancement and will contribute to your own goals in life, and in return you will work towards a career that is rewarding and flexible!
What will you have done before?   
- Min 3 years experience working with a range of stakeholders within the recruitment industry
- Excellent communication skills, both written & verbal
- Working autonomously & within a team, doing everything in your power to ensure your colleagues success as well as your own- recognising that the greater teams’ success will always benefit you personally
- Attention to detail and an enjoyment of being busy; managing multiple moving pieces at one time
- Min 3 years experience in a Business Development capacity or understanding of what is involved in this process
- A background in technology will be a huge bonus!

This role attracts a Base salary of $89,000- $100,000 Pkg + OTE

About the Role
We are seeking an experienced and dynamic Retail Store Manager to lead our store operations, drive sales growth and deliver a world-class customer experience. The successful candidate will be responsible for achieving commercial objectives, managing and developing the store team, maintaining brand and visual merchandising standards, and ensuring the efficient operation of the store.

Key Responsibilities
Sales and Customer Experience
* Manage store sales targets and monitor performance through relevant key performance indicators.

* Provide customers with accurate information regarding products, pricing, services and expected timeframes.
* Build strong customer relationships through personalised service and regular follow-up.
* Monitor customer feedback and implement initiatives to improve customer satisfaction.
* Build relationships with the local community and act as a brand ambassador to attract new customers and retain existing clients.
* Manage customer database development, segmentation and profiling.
* Drive in-store and omnichannel sales by effectively using available systems, tools and technology.

Business and Network Development
* Support the Area Manager in developing long-term market growth strategies.
* Establish and maintain commercial relationships and partnerships within the local market.
* Monitor relevant retail and industry trends.
* Identify and recommend sales opportunities and business development initiatives.

Brand and Product Management
* Represent and promote the company’s brand values, heritage and vision.
* Ensure employees have a strong understanding of the brand, products and services.
* Monitor the store’s product assortment and provide feedback to Area Management and the Buying Team regarding customer and market demand.
* Oversee the overall presentation of the store.
* Maintain high visual merchandising and product display standards in accordance with company guidelines.
* Ensure the team remains informed and trained on all product collections and categories.
Team Leadership and Human Resources
* Recruit, manage, develop, motivate and empower store employees.
* Build a positive and supportive workplace culture based on trust, professionalism and accountability.
* Provide ongoing coaching, feedback, training and performance development.
* Conduct daily and weekly store briefings to communicate objectives, priorities and sales strategies.
* Support new employees throughout the onboarding process.
* Ensure employees comply with company grooming and uniform standards.
* Work closely with the Area Manager and Human Resources team to recruit suitable employees.
* Manage employee performance and implement appropriate improvement measures where required.
* Prepare staff rosters and ensure appropriate staffing levels are maintained.

Store Operations and Compliance
* Supervise and coordinate all store activities to ensure efficient daily operations.
* Ensure compliance with the company’s standard operating procedures.
* Oversee stock and back-of-house operations, including receiving and transferring stock, stocktaking, stock control, storage, reporting and store administration.
* Ensure compliance with company policies, governance requirements, privacy obligations, workplace health and safety requirements and other applicable regulations.
* Use relevant retail, customer relationship management and point-of-sale systems.
* Ensure employees are appropriately trained in all operational and digital systems.

Skills and Experience
The successful candidate will have:
* Relevant experience managing a retail store or comparable retail operation.
* Demonstrated experience leading, developing and motivating a retail team.
* Strong knowledge of retail sales, customer service and store operations.
* Proven ability to achieve sales targets and manage key performance indicators.
* Experience in stock management, visual merchandising and operational compliance.
* Strong commercial awareness and problem-solving skills.
* Excellent communication, leadership and interpersonal skills.
* The ability to build strong relationships with customers, employees and business stakeholders.
* Experience using point-of-sale, customer relationship management and other retail management systems.
* The ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, customer-focused environment.

Experience in premium, luxury or fashion retail will be highly regarded.

In this role you will be responsible for the development of plans and techniques to meet our mining operations clients' needs. - Maintain a high degree of professionalism and diligence

- Develop engineering calculations, diagrams and technical reports
- Complete required technical and regulatory documents
- Ensure projects are completed on time and within the specified budget
- Present analysis results and project solutions to technical leads, senior leaders and clients as necessary
- Identify areas where improvements and savings could be made, or efficiencies generated
- Travel to sites operations as required

- 3+ years' related work exp.
- Bachelor's degree in mechanical, industrial, design or electrical engineering
- Drivers Licence
- Initiative in problem solving within assigned tasks
- Able to perform effectively within a team environment
- Demonstrated proficiency in written and verbal communication, including creating and delivering presentations
- Advanced skills in critical software applications
- Expertise in data and problem analysis, creative problem solving and design thinking

The role will manage assigned projects from start-to-finish, including design and documentation of equipment specifications. In addition, the Engineer will complete all tasks assigned by the Project Manager and/or Civil Manager, assisting with project specific reviews, conducting research, and writing reports. The intent of the role is to support operations in striving towards standardisation of tasks, removal of waste processes, increasing productivity and reduction of costs.

- Certificate IV OHS
- Section 44 Appointed Person
- Ability to pass a Pre-employment medical, incl. Drug & Alcohol screen
- 3+ years' experience in system and documentation development
- Excellent working knowledge of Microsoft Office packages, particularly Word and Excel
- A high attention to detail to ensure high quality work outcomes.

The following will also be highly regarded:
- Diploma of Occupational/Workplace Health and Safety
- 3+ years relevant mine site experience/crushing plants
- Previous machine operator experience.
- Cert IV Training and Assessment.

A remuneration package between $90,000 - $130,000 will be offered to the successful candidate

This position involves working in remote environments as part of a skilled wider-earthworks crew, ensuring all drainage infrastructure is constructed to specification, safely, and efficiently. You will be expected to have strong experience in trenching, pipe laying, Tailings Storage Facilities and reading construction plans, along with a solid understanding of site safety standards and environmental considerations. You will be expected to operate machines at times on drainage jobs but also when drainage works are intermittent on the rest of the project.

The role requires adaptability to demanding site conditions and a commitment to high-quality workmanship while maintaining productivity targets. A proactive attitude, strong teamwork skills, and the ability to work long shifts in remote FIFO conditions are essential for success in this role.

You will also need to demonstrate a minimum of 3 years work exp.

- Ideally be able to set out pipe alignments and levels using lasers and surveying equipment

- Operate and work around heavy machinery safely - during drainage works and during other TSF project works.
- Maintain tools, equipment, and a clean work environment

WHO IS PRA?   

PRA is a leading Digital & IT Recruitment company with offices in Brisbane, Sydney, Canberra and Melbourne.
  
PRA offers all its employees’ industry leading financial incentives, flexible working arrangements, training and genuine career growth in Melbourne and interstate.
 
Some of the key benefits are;

- High financial rewards with commission up to 50%
- Cloud based technology, so you can work from home or on the move
- External / Internal training and continuous improvement programs
- Career opportunities into management
- Work Perks such as up to 25 days leave per year, team events, lunch clubs, sales comps and many more.  
  
What is the role?   
Working out of our very cool Melbourne office, you will build your own accounts and networks. We will help you to develop your business and ensure your success as a best in class recruitment and technology professional.

You are able to work on both contract and permanent roles and you can build up significant revenue streams whilst placing permanent candidates. 
 
We have multiple positions available, such as:

- Candidate Manager 
- Associate Consultatant
- Recruitment Consultant
- Senior Consultant
- Managing Consultant
- Principal Consultant
- Client Services Manager 

Consultants within PRA are responsible to develop long term relationships with clients and to offer a professional and effective service to clients and candidates.  Delivery and the style of the delivery are paramount to maintain and develop the image of PRA as a leading supplier of recruitment solutions.

What will you do?
- Selling and promoting PRA’s services to existing and new customers
- Expanding PRA’s reach within each customer through business development activities
- Managing and maintaining client accounts for PRA’s services through consistent communication and client visits
- Assessing clients’ needs and providing services and solutions that satisfy client requirements
- Co-ordinating with PRA’s internal resources to ensure customers receive best in class service
- Providing timely and regular reporting to both internal and external stakeholders
- Utilising market knowledge to pitch new clients and win new business
- Dealing with clients & candidates, developing long term effective relationships
- Negotiating rates with clients, both contract and permanent
- Giving presentations to clients
- Handling clients and applicants through recruitment process to successful conclusion
- Writing advertisement copy
- Selection of applicants for vacancies
- Interviewing applicants
- Arranging interviews with clients and candidates
- Ensuring contact is made on a regular basis with contractors once placed out on the client’s site
- Maintaining awareness of trends within area of technical specialisation
- Ensuring that contact is made with clients on a regular basis and updating the database

What kind of person thrives in the PRA environment?   

Communication and people management are the defining elements of this role.  To perform it successfully, a candidate will need to be confident, and possess the ability to inform and persuade others and effectively present both themselves and the organisation they represent.  Friendliness and charisma are important factors in performing such a job effectively, together with the ability to put others at their ease.

Attention to detail, responsiveness and adaptability are also key elements in this job.  You will have energy and enthusiasm, and the ability to deal confidently with changes in work environments and situations.  The job often calls for work to meet deadlines or be completed within short timescales, and the ideal candidates will be prepared to commit themselves if they are to succeed.

Recruitment is challenging and fast-moving, and there are times you will practice patience to see through a difficult time or a minor repetitive task.  Having said this, you will see that these periods as necessary to your personal advancement and will contribute to your own goals in life, and in return you will work towards a career that is rewarding and flexible!
What will you have done before?   
- Min 3 years experience working with a range of stakeholders within the recruitment industry
- Excellent communication skills, both written & verbal
- Working autonomously & within a team, doing everything in your power to ensure your colleagues success as well as your own- recognising that the greater teams’ success will always benefit you personally
- Attention to detail and an enjoyment of being busy; managing multiple moving pieces at one time
- Min 3 years experience in a Business Development capacity or understanding of what is involved in this process
- A background in technology will be a huge bonus!

This role attracts a Base salary of $89,000- $100,000 Pkg + OTE 

Apply now for immediate consideration

NALHN serves over 400,000 people in northern Adelaide with a comprehensive range of high-quality healthcare services, including emergency, surgical, obstetric, neonatal, paediatric, oncology, geriatric, palliative care and rehabilitation, and mental health care, as well as primary health care services with a focus on community health promotion and chronic disease management.

What you will be doing
Two positions are offered, working within the Haematology Clinical Research Unit and Department of Haematology at Concord Hospital. The positions are open to qualified candidates in Clinical Haematology. Opportunities are available to develop your own research projects including enrolment in a higher research degree if desired. Fellows are encouraged to develop an area of research interest and to present at local, state and national meetings where appropriate. 

1.Clinical Research Unit (CRU) Fellow

a.The CRU Fellow manages patients treated in clinical trials across all haematological malignancies. They will gain valuable experience in managing patients treated with bispecific-trispecific antibodies and novel small molecules in phase I, II and III trials. They will work closely with the CAR T fellow in care of patients in CAR T trials.

b.They will provide both routine and urgent medical assessment and clinical care to patients screened & participating in clinical trials as a certified Investigator within Concord Haematology's Clinical Research Unit (CRU).

c.They will also be involved in supporting observational studies and disease registries.

2.Haemostasis & Thrombosis (H&T) Fellow

a.Management of patients on H&T clinical trials

b.Co-ordination of participants involved in H&T translational and observational research projects and registries. Potential for engagement with translational projects in collaboration with the ANZAC research institute.

c.Participation in specialty clinics: Inherited Platelet Disorders Clinic, clinics with Antiphospholipid Syndrome focus and general H&T clinics

d.Providing H&T consultative services within the hospital, including ICU H&T rounds, and coagulation laboratory support

e.Co-leading H&T governance activities including: VTE Prevention-Anticoagulation Stewardship meetings, Concord and District anticoagulation guideline updates

f.Providing rapid access outpatient service for management of acute VTE

The Concord Haematology Clinical Research Unit (HCRU)
Concord HCRU is a large and growing clinical research unit which supports Concord Haematology department goal to deliver "world class care locally". Housed in the purpose built Concord Cancer Centre, we undertake early to late phase clinical trials including CAR-T clinical trials and first-in-human phase I trials. The trials portfolio extends across a broad range of malignancies (lymphoma, leukaemia, myeloma, MDS) and other haematological disorders (thrombosis, autoimmune disorders). At any one time, the HCRU manages more than 120 studies either recruiting or in follow up from phase I-IV.

Under the leadership of the HCRU Haematologist Director and Manager, the HCRU supports 9 clinical haematologists and employs 13 clinical research nurses - study coordinators, 4 administrative staff responsible for ethics and regulatory requirements as well as 4 medical student data managers, and patient investigators. The Unit has a strong ethos of community engagement and its investigator-initiated research is supported by the Foundation for A Bloody Great Cause!

Where you will be working

Concord Repatriation General Hospital (CRGH) is a principal referral facility and a teaching hospital of the University of Sydney in the geographical centre of Sydney. CRGH offers a comprehensive range of specialty and sub-specialty services, many recognised nationally and internationally as Centre's of excellence. The affiliated ANZAC Research Institute performs high quality basic and translational research, in particular, the Platelet and Thrombosis Research Group led by Prof Vivien Chen.

Concord Haematology offers full clinical and laboratory services including autologous stem cell transplantation and apheresis unit, a large treatment and outpatient service as well as a general consultation service. Haematologists within the unit have strong ties to Working Groups in the Australasian Leukaemia and Lymphoma Group, representation on the Australasian Lymphoma Alliance and have many active national and international collaborations.

Based in Liverpool CBD, you will be part of a multidisciplinary Public Health Unit that includes Communicable Diseases, Immunisation, Environmental Health, and Administration teams, alongside Doctors, Nurses, Epidemiologists, and Data Quality Administrators dedicated to improving community health outcomes.

We are seeking a passionate nurse with a strong interest in public health and communicable disease management who thrives in a multidisciplinary team environment. You will possess exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to use telephone and other communication platforms to gather and convey critical information for the assessment and management of communicable diseases in an engaging, sensitive, and culturally appropriate manner. You will provide advice and support to healthcare professionals, aged care facilities, disability providers, schools, childcare centres, and other community stakeholders, helping to protect people and communities at risk of infection.

Join an organisation that is shaping the future direction of Neurosymbolic Artificial Intelligence in Australia, in an academic role that combines high-quality research, excellent teaching, and meaningful contribution to the School’s strategic priorities.

Job Details
•	Salary, 
o	Lecturer (Level B) – AUD $127,947 to $150,830 per annum + 17% superannuation

The Opportunity
Join the School of Computer Science and Engineering in the Faculty of Engineering at UNSW as a Lecturer / Senior Lecturer in a Teaching and Research role. In this role, you will contribute to the advancement of research and education in Neurosymbolic Artificial Intelligence, while helping to shape the next generation of AI researchers and practitioners.

You will conduct research in areas such as the integration of machine learning and symbolic reasoning to address complex and structured problems, and the development of robust and interpretable AI systems that advance the integration of learning and reasoning paradigms, contributing to high-impact research outcomes and the School’s growing research profile.

With established strengths in artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, and distributed systems, UNSW offers an exceptional environment for academics who are looking to build their research profile, contribute to collaborative research initiatives, and deliver high-quality teaching. You will contribute to the development of intelligent, interpretable, and trustworthy AI systems.

This is an opportunity to join a global leader in Computer Science, with cutting-edge facilities, world-class faculty, and an innovative research environment. With strong industry partnerships and a commitment to sustainability, UNSW provides excellent opportunities for career development, collaboration, and impact.

About You
You are an emerging or established academic with a strong foundation in Neurosymbolic Artificial Intelligence, with the ability to contribute to high-quality research and teaching. You bring expertise in areas such as machine learning and symbolic reasoning integration, knowledge representation, reasoning under uncertainty, and interpretable AI, and demonstrate the potential to build a strong research profile.

At Lecturer level (Level B), you will be developing your research profile and contributing to collaborative research activities, including competitive grant applications and scholarly publications, while also delivering high-quality teaching and supporting student learning across undergraduate and postgraduate courses.

At Senior Lecturer level (Level C), you will demonstrate an established research track record with evidence of research leadership, success in securing competitive funding, supervising HDR students, and making significant independent contributions to your field. You will also contribute to educational leadership through high-quality teaching, curriculum development, and mentoring students and colleagues.

You are an engaging educator with experience in delivering high-quality teaching and contributing to curriculum development. You are collaborative, adaptable, and motivated to contribute to a high-performing academic environment and to build strong relationships across academia and industry.

About UNSW

The Provisional Fellow will work in the NSW Biocontainment Centre (NBC), part of the NSW Specialist Service for High Consequence Infectious Diseases. The CMO will participate in the trainee roster as well as the clinical fellow roster as required. 
 
CMOs are responsible for the resuscitation-stabilisation of high risk newborn infants and for assessment, investigation, performing necessary procedure and formulating a management plan of admitted patients within the complex clinical environment of a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit as well as education, support and supervision of junior trainees. 
 

What you'll be doing

Responsibility for overall care of babies in the NICU until their discharge from the NICU.

Initial assessment of babies, and review of subsequent problems. Review of following results: blood gases, lab tests, X-rays & other investigations, including cerebral, cardiac and other ultrasounds. Plan management and therapy accordingly.

Procedures: Securing vascular access: intra-venous-intra-arterial. Performing arterial punctures, endotracheal intubations, insertion of intercostal catheters, lumbar punctures, needle aspiration of pneumothorax etc.; in particular teaching and supervising junior staff performing procedures

Attend morning and evening ward rounds with the nursing staff - Neonatologist on call - Trainee colleague-s, help formulate and execute plans for every baby. 

Attend all high-risk deliveries. 

Attend any unexpected neonatal emergencies in the delivery suite, operating theatres, post natal ward or elsewhere in Nepean Hospital.

Keep parents informed of the progress of their babies and also keep them abreast of any sudden deterioration in their baby's status.

Maintain, organise and update at least with each shift the patient notes and transcribe consultant comments from ward rounds. Examination of babies during your shift in Level 3 care and three times a week in Level 2 care.

Update regularly the Neonatal Database.

Assist the General Paediatric team with the resuscitation of babies less than 3 months corrected age in Nepean Hospital when required.

Where you'll be working

Nepean Hospital has an extremely active Perinatal Unit, ensuring a regular supply of high-risk deliveries within the hospital.

The NICU caters for more than 4,000 annual deliveries at the Nepean Hospital, as well as a number of transfers from other areas.

The NICU manages more than 1,000 admissions annually, about one third of these requiring Level 3 care.

Nepean NICU is a 37 bed department with currently 12 ventilated cots, up to 12 High-dependency (flex) cots and a separately located 16 bed Special Care Unit.

The NICU staff currently includes 6 full-time Staff Specialist Neonatologists, 3 CMOs, 1 Clinical Fellow and 9 Trainees.

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Essential requirements

MBBS or equivalent, currently registered with the Medical Board of Australia in an appropriate registration category.

Minimum four years' experience in a Level 3 Neonatal Intensive Care Unit with demonstrated ability to work at CMO level.

Demonstrated interest in performing point of care ultrasound.

This position is subject to an appropriate supervision level which can be supported by the health agency. If the incumbent's registration conditions include supervision requirements, the level of supervision must be able to be supported by the health agency for this role. 

Valid Working with Children Check, cleared National Police Check.

To be employed by NSW Health you are required to provide evidence of vaccination to comply with the NSW Health Occupational Assessment, Screening & Vaccination against Specified Infectious Diseases Policy, this includes any amendments made from time to time.

Selection criteria

Qualifications and experience commensurate with the Essential Requirements for the role.

Minimum four years' experience in a Level 3 Neonatal Intensive Care Unit with demonstrated ability to work at CMO level.

Demonstrated interest in performing point of care ultrasound.

Advanced ability to work collaboratively within multi-disciplinary teams, including the sharing of appropriate information internally and externally with key persons or services.

Advanced ability to work independently within a supervised complex clinical environment utilising excellent clinical skills, judgment and expertise.

Advanced verbal, written and interpersonal skills, with the capacity to vary communication style in line with the understanding of the needs of diverse audiences.

Advanced ability to prioritise workloads and display a flexible approach to meet changing situations in a demanding and unpredictable clinical environment.
